article: A Constrained Fuzzy Knowledge-Based System for the Management of Container Yard Operations

article: A Truck Scheduling Problem at a Cross-Docking Facility with Mixed Service Mode Dock Doors

Emerging requirements: The study indicates the need to incorporate truck-arrival and load uncertainty, relax the unlimited temporary-storage assumption, and model door-front and server-capacity constraints to obtain a more realistic cross-docking planning scheme.

article: Dynamic Appointment Rescheduling of Trucks under Uncertainty of Arrival Time
Logistic focus: gate operations, queue / congestion management, reactive rescheduling, truck scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize the comprehensive operating costs of truck companies and port companies, explicitly including truck re-scheduling costs, gate waiting costs, and idle-emission costs.
Performance metrics reported: computational time, queue length, total cost
Limitations/gaps: The study uses a fixed time-window distribution rule in which a truck that is late in the last appointment window cannot make a new reservation, although in real operations trucks may still enter after the nominal window. It also assumes that a successfully booked truck will eventually arrive and does not model post-booking no-shows.
Emerging requirements: Future work should allow more realistic handling of trucks arriving after the last window and explicitly incorporate the probability of no-show after reservation, with better strategies to minimize reservation-plan adjustments.

article: Adaptive Real-Time Planning of Trailer Assignments in High-Throughput Cross-Docking Terminals
Logistic focus: cross-docking operations, inbound-outbound synchronization, reactive rescheduling, truck scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize inbound and outbound trailer waiting times and tardiness through adaptive trailer-to-dock assignment, while improving synchronized flows, dock utilization, and overall makespan.
Technical artifact delivered: decision support system, exact algorithm, hybrid optimization framework, mathematical model
Performance metrics reported: computational time, makespan, resource utilization, tardiness, waiting time
Limitations/gaps: The framework depends on accurate real-time data streams, and data latency, missing values, or inconsistent updates may degrade solution quality. In addition, the MILP remains tractable only for the tested mid-size scenario, so larger terminals may require stronger solver strategies, heuristics, or parallel computing. The transportation phase is also externalized, with routing effects entering only through ETA updates rather than integrated optimization.
Emerging requirements: The study indicates the need for more scalable solution methods for larger hubs, tighter integration of live ETA/routing information, and robust deployment over real IoT-driven terminal data streams for continuous adaptive re-optimization.

article: Multi-Door Cross-Dock Scheduling under Flexible Doors Mode and Material Handling Resource Restrictions
Logistic focus: cross-docking operations, inbound-outbound synchronization, truck scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize total departure tardiness, modeled as total delay penalties of outbound trucks, while jointly deciding truck-to-door schedules and, in the DFA variant, forklift allocation.
Technical artifact delivered: exact algorithm, hybrid optimization framework, mathematical model, metaheuristic
Limitations/gaps: The DFA setting requires a minimum number of forklifts to obtain near-optimal solutions in reasonable time, and the study leaves insufficiently explored more restrictive settings with simultaneous shortage of doors and forklifts, as well as mixed-door performance under unforeseen inbound disruptions.
Emerging requirements: The paper points to stronger solution methods for the DFA model, deeper analysis of cross-docks with both fewer doors and fewer forklifts, and evaluation of mixed-door operation under unexpected truck-arrival disruptions.

article: Integrating Arrival Time Estimation in Truck Scheduling: An Explorative Study in Grocery Retailing
Logistic focus: queue / congestion management, reactive rescheduling, truck scheduling, yard resource scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize the expected sum of truck waiting times throughout the working day by periodically reassigning incoming trucks to unloading resources using up-to-date ETA, processing times, and current warehouse-resource status.
Technical artifact delivered: decision support system, heuristic, mathematical model
Limitations/gaps: The model assumes fixed unloading resources during the day, which restricts adherence to alternative warehouse-door environments and operational characteristics. The empirical comparison is only against FCFS, and the study does not include an economic evaluation of implementation costs and overall benefits.
Emerging requirements: Future work should relax the fixed-resource assumption, compare the approach with scheduling rules beyond FCFS, study different rescheduling frequencies and alternative strategies such as event-driven rescheduling, and perform a fuller economic evaluation for both carrier and receiving facility.

article: Inbound Truck Scheduling for Workload Balancing in Cross-Docking Terminals
Logistic focus: cross-docking operations, queue / congestion management, reactive rescheduling, truck scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize workload imbalance in temporary inventory storage across outbound chutes and total waiting time of inbound trucks through dynamic inbound truck scheduling.
Technical artifact delivered: hybrid optimization framework, mathematical model, simulation model
Limitations/gaps: The model assumes homogeneous cargo, ignores internal travel time from the arrival point to the dock, and uses a very large temporary chute-storage capacity, which suppresses terminal shutdown effects caused by severe congestion; the paper also notes that incomplete information and real uncertainty may reduce practical solution quality.
Emerging requirements: The study points to integrating outbound-truck information with inbound scheduling, handling heterogeneous cargo and uncertain arrivals/service times, incorporating bottleneck-induced shutdowns under limited temporary storage, and validating the approach in large-scale multi-terminal real operations.

article: Modelling Cross-Docking in a Three-Level Supply Chain with Stochastic Service and Queuing System: {{MOWFA}} Algorithm
Logistic focus: cross-docking operations, inbound-outbound synchronization, queue / congestion management, truck scheduling
Modeling objective: Minimize total operational cost and total transfer/waiting time across the three-level supply chain, including location-fixed costs, transportation costs, cross-dock costs, transfer time, and product waiting time in cross-docks.
Technical artifact delivered: hybrid optimization framework, mathematical model, metaheuristic
Performance metrics reported: computational time, total cost, waiting time
Limitations/gaps: The paper explicitly notes that the problem is NP-hard and that solution time increases sharply with instance size. In addition, the operational model neglects storage costs because items are assumed to be sent as soon as they are packaged, and the empirical validation is restricted to randomly generated instances rather than a reported case study.
Emerging requirements: The study indicates the need for more efficient solution methods for larger NP-hard instances and for extensions that bring the model closer to real-world cross-docking conditions, since the authors frame current research gaps as a lack of sufficiently realistic models.
